title: Rabbi Avin, Father of Rabbi Avin HaLevi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman quotes the old Tanchuma, Tazria: “Rabbi Avin his father said, in the name of Rabbi Abba bar Kahana: The Holy One, blessed be He, does not measure all at once,” etc. Buber’s text reads “Rabbi Avin HaLevi.” Hyman reports that Buber cites the Rome manuscript and the manuscript abbreviated רח״ם for the reading “Rabbi Avin, the father of Rabbi Avin HaLevi.”

notes.text: The abbreviation רח״ם remains literal and unidentified; it is not securely expanded as Rabbi Chaim. The father reading follows the supplied heading and remains qualified. This notice is held for that unresolved source expression.

Buber’s Tanchuma, Tazria §8 (p. 36, note מד), gives “Rabbi Avin, father of Rabbi Avin HaLevi” for the Rome manuscript and MS רח״ם. In the printed version Buber compares, “his father” lacks the identifying words that follow it in those manuscripts. In his introduction under Manuscript D, Buber identifies the abbreviation left unresolved in the preceding note: רח״ם designates the Oxford manuscript formerly in Chaim Michael’s collection. The consulted Hebrew Tanchuma, Tazria §6, reads “Rabbi Avin his father” and “does not measure all at once.” Buber’s main text names Rabbi Avin HaLevi and gives “in a basket” as its corrected reading. Hyman’s printed article (vol. I, p. 93) reads אביו של, “the father of,” where the supplied transcription has אבין של. The family relationship is reported as a manuscript reading.
